results.reasoning: Built under a temp WALKDOWN_HOME: a repo with a root home (`repo`), a pack inside it with its own (`pack`), a symlink outside the pack at $T/link pointing at the pack's home, and a hand-written row `link` (no `registered:`, project = the tree between, home = the link) appended to registry.yml (01). Three of the four THEN clauses held. `where --blueprint link` sets the row aside and says it was written by hand; `status` and `thread new --as-agent` through it exit 2 with no blueprint for `link`, and no thread or run file appeared anywhere under the fixture (02). A server at the repo root on 4731 listed exactly `repo` and `pack`, answered 404 to `?bp=link` and to the link's path spelled as a key, and refused POST /api/threads through both, again writing nothing (03). Standing at the root reaches `repo`, in the pack (and deeper) reaches `pack`, and standing in the tree between - where I planted an unregistered .walkdown declaring `between`, and which the hand row's project names - reaches `repo`; `--blueprint between` finds nothing (06). The import clause failed: with the hand row present, `walkdown import $T/link` (four spellings, including relative and trailing slash) and even `walkdown import <the real home path>` all print `already listed ... as \`link\`` and register nothing, so `walkdown blueprints` shows only `repo` and standing in the pack reaches the root's row, while every import insists the pack is listed (04, 05). The already-listed check in the bare-home add (bin/commands/blueprint.js ~148) and in rememberInRegistry (lib/locations.js ~445) searches every row rather than the registered ones and compares canon(expand(r.home)) - resolving the hand row's link on read and following it. With the hand row removed, the same import registers the pack once under its real path and a second import says already listed, so the mechanism is right and only the set-aside row leaks into it. Filed as n-0278.
